title: Stress chronicle: dedicated capacity orchestration, throughput scenarios, and customer acceptance
creator: Asha Patel
description: Create an end-to-end orchestration and test plan for validating dedicated capacity throughput guarantees, autoscaling policies, and fleet controls against realistic customer workloads. Deliverables: a reproducible scenario runner, a set of benchmark methodologies (ramp/stable/tail-focused), and a documented customer acceptance test suite + pass/fail criteria.
background: Customers buying Dedicated capacity expect predictable throughput and graceful autoscale/fallback behavior. Existing artifacts (various harnesses and prober scripts) are fragmented across repos; results differ by synthetic load profile and cache warmup state. This ticket consolidates an orchestration playbook that codifies how we measure, certify, and hand off throughput guarantees to customers.
scope: Design and implement: 1) scenario definitions that reflect production prompt-length and token distributions, 2) an orchestration runner to execute multi-node stress runs with KV-cache warmup, 3) standardized metrics, dashboards and artifacts for customer acceptance, 4) documented runbook for edge cases (OOM, fallback to smaller model variants).
non_goals: We will not re-architect the runtime in this ticket. We will not build new model quantization tooling (only annotate existing quant profiles). We will not onboard every historical customer workload — pick 3 representative workload classes for the first pass.
success_metrics: Reproducible throughput claims: run results can be replayed within ±10% across 3 independent runs
Tail latency SLO: p99 <= SLA_target_ms for certified runs (per-customer SLA variable)
Autoscale correctness: scale-up and scale-down actions occur within configured windows and do not cause >5% request failures during transition
Artifact completeness: single run emits artifacts (load config, traces, perf metrics, flamegraphs, billing counters, run summary) to the designated storage location
acceptance_criteria: Scenario runner supports: production-like token length distribution, KV cache priming, multiple model variants, and synthetic TPS control
Benchmark methodology doc reviewed and approved by Performance and SRE leads
Three representative scenarios executed end-to-end: short-chat, long-context-generation, embedding-batch; each has defined ramp, sustain, and cooldown phases
Customer acceptance checklist created with pass/fail thresholds and verification commands
test_plan: Define workload profiles: derive token length and prompt distribution from production traces (anonymized) or synthetic proxy if no trace available
Create config per scenario: target_qps, concurrency, request size histogram, KV-cache warmup steps
Execute warmup: bootstrap KV caches by replaying a 10-minute primer at 20% target load
Ramp phase: increase load linearly over 5 minutes to target_qps
Sustain phase: run at target_qps for 30 minutes to measure steady-state throughput and GPU utilization
Tail-focused run: run short bursts to capture p99+/p999 behavior and observe autoscale triggers
Scale-down observation: after sustain, drop to 10% and observe scale-down cooldowns and behavior
Failure modes: induce a single-node OOM and verify graceful fallback policies (route to spare pool or downgrade model) and that customers see documented degradation behavior
Collect artifacts: prometheus timeseries, per-token latencies, kernel utilization, per-instance billing counters, logs, and flamegraphs
Post-run analysis: aggregate three runs, compute variance, generate summary PDF and dashboard snapshot
orchestration_playbook: Runner: k8s Job + stepper controller that manipulates client load generators (wrk2-derived) and ensures KV warmup state across pod restarts
Profiles: YAML workload definitions; include token distribution, prompt templates, and failure-injection knobs
Autoscaling test harness: orchestrate cluster-level scale events by toggling node pools and injecting synthetic load spikes
Metric collection: ensure tracing hook creates a run_id and all emitters tag with run_id; use central S3 path for artifacts
Cost accounting: sample per-run billing counters and convert to per-token cost for reporting to sales/customers
